v: A big-occasion, big-price Xerjoff. The note list reads like a cashmere coat with a cinnamon roll in the pocket. At this price you sample first, full stop.
A long spice-and-resin list that reads like a mood board for a very serious dinner. The notes promise leather and oud, so sample it and see how heavy you like your heavy.
Rose, orris and resins over a mossy base, which is a lot of old-world glamour on paper. Sample it, because this is a scent for people who like their drydown with a backstory.

n: Amouage Interlude Man Eau de Parfum
v: Amouage's famously loud, smoky one. Wearers either call it a masterpiece or a house fire. Find out which camp you're in for the price of a sample.
Rosemary and neroli up top, vetiver and sandalwood underneath, so the notes promise tidy and grown-up. Sample it first and find out if tidy is your signature.
Mandarin blossom, pear, jasmine, iris, then a woody-amber finish: the notes promise understated. Sample it, since quiet scents are the hardest ones to judge from a list.
The boozy holiday-party scent. Gorgeous in December, a lot in July. Sample it and wear it on a cold day before committing.
Ginger and cardamom into Turkish rose, then vanilla and benzoin, so the list reads warm and a little dessert-adjacent. Sample it before you commit to 50 ml of extrait.
The 'is it even on?' scent, in a good way. Some people barely smell it on themselves, so a sample is mandatory before paying Le Labo prices.

n: Apple Brandy On The Rocks Eau de Parfum
v: The notes read like a very good cocktail menu: apple, rum, brandy, vanilla. Sample it, because sweet and boozy is a love-it-or-lose-it proposition.
Clean white T-shirt energy. Pleasant, easy, office-safe; whether it's worth luxury money is a question for your wrist, not the internet.
Two kinds of rose, two kinds of jasmine, and olibanum underneath, so it is not shy about being a rose. Sample it and see if you want your florals this extra.
The scent of every elevator since 2017. Instantly recognizable, which is either the point or the problem. A 1 to 2 ml sample tells you which.
A Byredo bestseller. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample before paying full-bottle prices.
Peach and plum over violet, then leather and vanilla, which is Dark Academia in a bottle if the notes deliver. Sample it before deciding whether it is cozy or just sweet.

n: Tom Ford Black Orchid Eau de Parfum
v: Tom Ford's entry-level goth era. Polarizing by design, which is exactly why you sample it before you buy it.
A By Kilian with big fans and big prices. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample first.
Byredo's crisp, clean, laundered-linen scent. Lovely, subtle, and the kind of thing that smells different on everyone. Sample it.

n: Penhaligon's Blenheim Bouquet Eau de Toilette

v: Peppers and juniper over sandalwood and vetiver, so the notes lean dry and woody. Sample it first; a list this tidy can be either elegant or forgettable.
A quieter Parfums de Marly than the famous ones. Promising notes, less hype, so test it before you trust it.
Watermelon, tuberose, musk: a three-note list for a scent wearers often call a big white floral. Sample it, because tuberose is the one note people regret blind buying.
The library lists only the top notes (coriander, carnation, pepper, saffron), so we can't tell you the drydown yet. That's reason enough to sample before spending a Xerjoff-sized sum.
A citrus-and-woods scent that wearers often bring up in the same breath as Aventus. Sample it on its own merits before committing to 120 ml.

n: Creed Aventus For Her Eau de Parfum

v: Not a perfume, a car payment. Wearers describe pineapple and birch over smoky musk, and argue forever about batches. A sample tells you if you're an Aventus person or just watched too much 2016 YouTube.
Creed's sea-breeze-and-pine one. Bright, outdoorsy, and priced like a yacht. Sample it on a hot day.

n: Creed Green Irish Tweed Eau de Parfum
v: The original Creed status scent, before Aventus took the crown. Classic in the best and slightly-dad ways. Sample it, then shop around: bottle prices vary a lot.
A lesser-worn Creed. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample before paying Creed prices.
A crisp, grown-up vetiver. Quietly great, rarely hyped. Sample it if you like fresh-and-woody over sweet.
Creed's oud. We haven't confirmed its note list yet, and it's one of the priciest per ml in our library. Sample first, obviously.

n: Creed Royal Water Eau de Parfum
Creed Silver Mountain Water Eau de Parfum
v: Mountain-stream energy. Fresh, metallic, a little old-school. Sample it, because 'fresh' at Creed prices needs to be the right fresh.

n: Creed Tabarome Millesime Eau de Parfum

v: Creed's peppery, minty one. Interesting on paper; test it on skin before trusting a note list with this much money.
A soft, sweet Creed floral. Pretty and approachable; bottle prices swing wildly between shops, so sample, then compare.

n: Parfums de Marly Delina Eau de Parfum
v: The pink bottle every girlie on your feed owns. Rose-and-lychee, polished, very popular. Sample it, then buy the bigger bottle: the small one is a commitment-issues tax.
Palo santo, incense, leather, cade oil and ebony: the notes promise a smoldering mood. Sample it, because smoke is flattering on exactly some people.
Lavender and bergamot up top, coffee in the heart, leather and incense below: a gentleman's club with a very long list. Sample it first, since a note list this long can go anywhere.
A fruit-salad-with-vanilla-on-top scent that projects for days. Fun, loud, love-or-hate. Sample it before your coworkers have to.

n: Fan Your Flames Extrait de Parfum
v: Coconut and rum over tobacco and tonka, so the notes promise a beach bar after hours. Sample it before committing 50 ml of extrait to a vacation mood.

n: Geranium Pour Monsieur Eau de Parfum

v: Rose and orange over nutmeg and cinnamon, then sandalwood and vanilla. Sample it; the name promises a look, and the drydown should deliver the rest.
Lavender and orange up top, cinnamon and clove in the heart, then vanilla and amber. Wearers often call it a warm, bedroom-ish scent, so sample it before you make it your office signature.
Lavender and clary sage, bitter almond and orris, then leather and tonka. The name is doing a lot of the work, so sample it and see if the scent keeps up.

n: Gentle Fluidity Gold Eau de Parfum
v: A cozy, musky vanilla from Kurkdjian. Comfortable and easy; sample it to see if it's special on you or just nice.
Thyme, saffron and raspberry over leather and blond woods, which is an unusual list. Sample it, because unusual lists are where blind buys go to die.

n: Good Girl Gone Bad Eau de Parfum
v: A full-glam white floral with a name built for TikTok. Pretty, heady, pricey. Sample it first.
Campfire-in-a-pine-forest, but make it Scandinavian. Easy to love; sample it, then compare sizes, because the big bottle is much better value per ml.
Aventus's cooler cousin who moved to Portland. Often recommended to Aventus fans; sample both side by side.
A lavender that went to finishing school. Interesting, pricey, not for everyone. Sample it.
Leather-armchair-in-a-Nancy-Meyers-movie energy. A winter scent for most people; sample it before committing to 125 ml of it.
Almond and magnolia over vanilla and sandalwood, listed as a floral amber. Sample it, since white florals with almond tend to divide the room.
Amouage's Jubilation 25, with a note list we haven't confirmed yet. Sample it first; a name that happy deserves a verdict from your own skin.

n: Penhaligon's Juniper Sling Eau de Toilette
L'Ombre dans l'Eau Eau de Parfum

v: Parfums de Marly's crowd-pleaser and a forum favorite. Very likeable, very common. Sample it to see if likeable is enough.

n: Love, Don't Be Shy Eau de Parfum
v: A candy-sweet orange blossom with serious fans. Sweetness tolerance varies a lot; sample it.
The library has amber and ambergris and nothing else yet, so treat anything beyond that as unconfirmed. Sample it before committing 90 ml to a list this short.

n: Maison Margiela Replica Bubble Bath Eau de Toilette
Maison Margiela Replica Lazy Sunday Morning Eau de Toilette

v: Blackcurrant and raspberry, rose and jasmine tea, then vanilla and praline. Sample it, because a sweet fruity floral is either your joy or your headache.
A breezy, polished Creed citrus. Nice in summer, priced for all seasons. Sample it; we haven't found a buyable US bottle yet.
Smells-like-expensive-skin territory. Soft and wearable; sample it to check it doesn't vanish on you.

n: Tom Ford Ombré Leather Eau de Parfum
v: Tom Ford's leather jacket in a bottle. A modern classic for leather lovers; sample it, then shop around.
Turkish rose and ylang over nutmeg, leather and amber, then patchouli, vanilla and vetiver. Sample it; the name promises theater and the drydown has to earn the curtain call.
Citrus and berries up top, then marshmallow, Chantilly cream and musk, so the notes read like a dessert menu. Sample it, since sweet this deliberate is a taste, not a given.
The oud people warn you about. Loud and proud. Never blind buy an oud; sample it.

n: Oud for Happiness Eau de Parfum
Oud Satin Mood Eau de Parfum
v: Velvet robe in a Bridgerton ballroom. Rich, heavy, gorgeous on the right person. Sample it in cool weather.

n: Oud Silk Mood Extrait de Parfum
v: Kurkdjian's extrait oud and the priciest sample in our library. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample first.
A Parfums de Marly with a loyal following. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample first.
A fresher Parfums de Marly. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; start with a sample.
A grand, dramatic rose that wears like a velvet cape. A classic, and a lot. Sample it before you commit.
Bergamot and ylang, Bulgarian rose and heliotrope, then myrrh and sandalwood. Sample it, because the name sets expectations the list alone can't confirm.

n: Replica Autumn Vibes Eau de Toilette
Replica Beach Walk Eau de Toilette
Replica Coffee Break Eau de Toilette
Replica Jazz Club Eau de Toilette
v: A smoky-bar scent with a devoted following. Sample it before you commit; it's a very specific mood.

n: Replica Under the Lemon Trees Eau de Toilette
v: Lime, petitgrain and cardamom over green tea and white musks, so the notes read fresh and calm. Sample it first; fresh scents are the ones that vanish on skin for some people.
A very long note list, from lemon and thyme to galbanum, leather and ambergris. Sample it first, since this much going on is either a masterwork or a lot.

n: Rolling in Love Eau de Parfum
v: Almond milk, iris and freesia over tuberose, vanilla and tonka. Sample it before you let the almond milk decide for you.
A Le Labo rose. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; at Le Labo prices, sample first.
The scent of every downtown hotel lobby since 2014. Iconic is an overused word, but here it fits, for better and worse. Sample it.
Parfums de Marly's fresh one. A strong summer pick; sample it to see if it earns a place in your rotation.
A boozy Initio with a cult following. We haven't confirmed its note list yet; sample first.
Pencil-shavings-in-a-good-way. Subtle and minimal; we haven't found a US sample source yet.
Fig, bay leaf and bergamot over cedar and vetiver, then tobacco and hay. Sample it first; the name says tea, the notes say something smokier.
Whiskey and spice over tobacco, oud, incense and vanilla. Sample it; the notes promise a lot of atmosphere, and atmosphere is skin-dependent.

n: Tom Ford Bois Pacifique Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Cherry Smoke Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Costa Azzurra Eau de Parfum
Private Blend Italian Cypress Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Jasmin Rouge Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Neroli Portofino Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Noir de Noir Eau de Parfum
v: Full villain-arc rose. Dark, rich, Private Blend pricing. Sample it.
The gentlest door into oud. Smooth, office-safe for an oud, and much better value per ml in the big bottle once you know it's yours.

n: Tom Ford Rose de Chine Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Soleil Blanc Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Tobacco Vanille Eau de Parfum
v: Cabin-in-a-Nancy-Meyers-movie energy. Rich and sweet; sample it in winter, then buy the big bottle if it's your signature.

n: Tom Ford Tuscan Leather Eau de Parfum
v: Raspberry and leather, loud and luxe. A classic for leather fans; sample it.

n: Tom Ford Vanille Fatale Eau de Parfum
Tom Ford Venetian Bergamot Eau de Parfum

v: Mojito-on-a-patio energy. Bright and fun; sample it to see if it lasts on you.
Honey-tobacco with a Sicilian tan. A forum favorite; sample it before paying Xerjoff prices.
